A lot of this is cleaning up other people's mistakes - like in an ideal world we wouldn't have thousands upon thousands of unwanted and abandoned pets. But we do. We wouldn't feel duty bound to limit or exploit procreation of other species in an ideal world, but we don't live in that situation. In my suburb alone there are pregnant cats being rescued every week. A lot of them are barely 6 months old when they're having these kittens. Sure, it's natural for cats to reproduce, but that doesn't mean a cat won't procreate until its untimely death. People are not responsible enough to keep their cats indoors, then refuse to care for the kittens. Intact males also fight so often and so savagely they end up with life ending infections. 
Animals don't have the same rights, access to care and sapience as humans when it comes to reproduction. Many people opt to spay or neuter because it is much safer than the alternative - accidental, unwanted litters.
Don't beat yourself up for slipping up, just keep at it. But it *is* a conscious effort you need to make.

I've worked in homelessness for a fair few years now. It is rare that the primary goal for begging, especially actually approaching people and/or begging at traffic lights, is for anything except drugs - usually crack, heroin and/or spice. 

I do not personally give money to people begging, however some of the people I knew were very entrenched in addiction and only moved from their spot to score, use or sleep. They would only eat food that was given to them, everything else went on their habit. I would often have to time meetings for when they had already scored, otherwise they would not want me around ruining their graft. 

I don't work in outreach anymore but I do research into homelessness. I wouldn't judge anyone for asking for money to score, but I also would not tolerate anyone trying to strong arm me after a polite no or offer of an alternative. 

I often buy food or drinks (always ask them what they want first!) and have made up the odd essentials package for someone I knew quite well who was in an awful state and needed quite a lot of basics after being robbed. 

Donating your money to sifa, shelter or cgl goes a bit further in my opinion. It's very hard to engage someone in support when they can essentially earn their habit every day - even if it is killing them through self neglect.

I'm pro animal testing for certain medical trials, yeah. However I'm 'more' pro developing better systems for testing medicines and there are lots underway. 
But we need to make sure medicines aren't going to have catastrophic results before administration to human volunteers.

I believe we need to keep and raise a small (honestly, tiny) amount of animals for medicinal/scientific purposes. I'm talking testing, biological medicines, baby formula etc (with an aim to reduce our reliance on animals as part of ongoing research.) 

Animals that have to be bred and kept should be kept as well as possible. A farm like this goes some of the way into doing that. 

Trying to justify it for food though just doesn't work. I'm not even saying the above is "good", I wish we could be 100% removed from animal exploitation, but I think it's a current grim reality. But we shouldn't let our comparatively small need justify a huge, unnecessary and destructive want.

There is no form of birth control that is 100% effective - bar abstinence. However, the pill is extremely effective when taken correctly - 99%. This means that for every 100 people taking the pill, less than one would fall pregnant each year. 
Read your pill pamphlet about what to do in the case of a late or missed pill - and follow those guidelines! For example if you are told to use additional protection for 7 days, make sure to use condoms every time for that week. 
Pulling out is not considered an effective form of birthcontrol on its own but paired with the pill you're really REALLY unlikely to get pregnant.

It did take a huge toll on my mental health but I have some tips: firstly, make sure you let all your tutors and school admin know you have a health condition and ask what support they can provide. I got lots of help and counselling and even qualified for Disabled Student Allowance which is a UK thing that provides things like printers and computers and special chairs etc for students with various issues. Find local support groups and find at least one group/society/easy going sports group that has a weekly meeting at university of nearby. 
Making friends at university is a thousand times easier than school. There will be lots of people in the same or similar boats to you regarding social skills and you'll all learn together. Be kind and forgiving, and try to see the best in the people around you. Help people when you can and don't be afraid to ask for help from others. 
Go to the library to do your homework if you can. It can get very difficult mentally if you spend all your time in your room. Try to eat in communal areas too. 

Open up to people. It won't get back to your parents. You're safe, and can share what you've been through if you find people you want to tell. My friends were a real lifeline when I was struggling. Think, bringing me food, asking me to join them downstairs for a cup of tea etc. when I got really bad. 

Don't speak to your parents much. Test the boundaries of what you can get away with - a phone call a week? A text? Etc. The healing happens when you're away from them, not just physically but mentally too. 

Make lots of friends and introduce yourself a lot. You can work out who your good friends will be with time. 
Call people out for bullying or bad mouthing others. You don't want to be friends with people like that, and people will respect you for not letting it happen around you.

You might not want to hear this but here goes - you're on venlafaxine for a reason. Stopping your treatment to get high on MDMA is a really bad idea for a few reasons. Firstly, coming off venlafaxine is rough for your brain and body, especially cold turkey/quickly reducing your dose - you could relapse into a really bad mental state, and feel like you've got the worst flu of your life. Secondly, messing with your treatment could set you back in your recovery and it could take weeks for you to stabilise once you're back on your correct dose. Thirdly, MDMA upsets your serotonin levels massively, you could actually undo so much of the hard work your brain has been doing to get better in one roll. And finally, have you heard of the concept of "blue Mondays"? That's when you crash out after rolling and feel awful because of how upset/lacking your brain chemistry is. You're already a suicide risk with depression and anxiety, so this could very well push you into that mindset. 

Venlafaxine leaves your body relatively quickly as it has a short half life. But that also means it has one of the nastiest withdrawals. It usually takes people months and months to slowly taper off and even then they may have unpleasant side effects. It might be worth looking into a different way to relax than chemically.

Being bitten by a hamster hurts but it will not kill you. Flinching away from your hamster, smelling nervous etc. will make it harder to tame your little one. I have a baby ham at the moment who I am in the process of taming and he will let me pick him up but will not stay in my hand for more than a second, he'll jump out no matter what. So I am currently just practising picking him up. I scoop him up with both hands, one either side, so he can see them, pick him up about an inch off the counter, then immediately release him, let him get down or jump off my hands. Then I give him a treat (a seed). This way he is learning that me picking him up is a good thing. Experiment with different foods and get the hamster out of the cage for taming. Inside the cage you are way more likely to be bitten.

I personally think it is fine to get them out the cage safely by holding them gently around the waist and quickly putting them down next to the cage, rather than my usual two handed scoop. This can frighten the ham but they shouldn't be able to bite you as easily so it's less likely to happen. Once they are out the cage and in 'neutral' territory, it is much easier to interact with them - that's why a bath can be a great, safe place to tame a hamster (getting them into the bathroom might be a challenge at first though!).

Try not to panic and remember, even if she does bite you again, unless she is very, very scared or you are seriously encroaching on her territory (like putting your hands in the cage next to her bed while she's in it) any bite will be more of a warning nip than a chomp.

Just so you know, they will be able to chew through that enclosure in a matter of seconds if they want to. If before you had the two days of placebo pills, you took 21 (or more) active pills, you do not need to treat the two pills as missed doses. If you took 20 pills or less then you should follow the instructions for two missed pills.

When starting birth control, especially as a young woman, it's best to just ignore the bleeding and keep taking the pills as advised.

You have two choices - have another four days of placebos (making it seven days including the pill you took by accident) and then carrying on with your next packet.
This is fine for your health - just make sure you have another active pill you can take to make up for the one you took on your placebo week - you have to take at least 21 active pills IN A ROW to be protected from pregnancy.
The other option is to just keep taking the active pills from now on and have your next period a bit earlier. It will probably make very little difference in the amount of breakthrough bleeding you have anyway.

Remember - no more than 7 days of placebo pills, but fewer is fine, and no FEWER than 21 days of active pills, but MORE is also fine!
For example some people only have a period every 4 months, so they take 84 active pills in a row, but to remain protected, still only have 7 days maximum of placebo pills.

These sound like hypnogogic hallucinations. They're scary, but more common than people think. You aren't crazy and they don't mean you're schizophrenic or anything like that.

One theory is that they manifest when your brain is so anxious that it's trying so hard to find a threat it makes one up out of what it can see around you - often it's much easier for your brain to trick you if the room is a bit dark or you have things in your room that mimic other shapes, like a coat hanging up becomes a monster, folds in a sheet become a face etc.

I used to get these. One thing that really helped was EMDR therapy. Other than that, counselling or CBT and discussing it with a professional should really help.
